question: RBI cuts repo rate by 50 bps. Which sector MOST likely sees stock prices decline short-term?
before: Rate cuts mean banks must lower lending rates. If lending rates fall faster than deposit rates, NIM compresses hurting earnings. Real estate benefits (cheaper loans). IT neutral to Indian rates. FMCG rate-insensitive.
after:
Concept: Net Interest Margin (NIM) is the difference between the average yield a bank earns on its assets (loans) and the average rate it pays on its liabilities (deposits). When the RBI cuts the repo rate, banks face pressure to lower lending rates immediately, but deposit rates typically adjust downward more slowly, causing NIM to compress and reducing profitability.

Why this is correct: Banking sector stock prices are most vulnerable to short-term declines after a repo rate cut because NIM compression directly reduces net interest income, the largest component of bank earnings. The market immediately reprices bank valuations downward on rate-cut announcements due to visible earnings headwinds.

Why the others are wrong:

A) Real estate actually benefits short-term from cheaper borrowing costs, supporting demand for mortgages and project financing. Stock prices in this sector typically rise or remain stable after rate cuts.

B) IT services have minimal direct exposure to domestic Indian interest rates. Their earnings depend on dollar-denominated export revenues and global tech spending, making them essentially neutral to RBI policy shifts.

D) FMCG companies are rate-insensitive because consumer staple demand is inelastic and their business models rely on pricing power and volume, not on financing costs or cost of capital.

Intuition: Equity analysts must recognize that rate cuts are mechanically negative for bank earnings in the short run due to NIM compression, even though they may support broader economic growth. This creates a tactical trading opportunity: banks typically underperform on rate-cut days, but valuations may recover if management credibly guides on deposit cost management or volume growth offsets margin pressure.
